alex_ng: Quick question — how should the rerank endpoint behave when a caller sends more candidates than their top_k? e.g. candidates=500, top_k=10. truncate? error? do we charge for all 500?
priya_chowdhury: I vote: accept, compute scores for all, return top_k. But we need clear quota semantics — charging per candidate scored, not per returned item. Otherwise users will craft big lists to game things. :thinking_face:
jun_li: compute-all is expensive on high-fanout. Could we offer two modes: `strict` (error if >max_candidates) and `best-effort` (truncate to max_candidates) and make default `best-effort`? console can show a warning when truncation happens.
kelsey: For rollout we should avoid breaking callers. Default should be tolerant. Error mode can be an opt-in strict flag for internal teams.
yuri: Telemetry needs an event for "candidate_truncated" with original_count, processed_count, and model_variant. Also track whether truncation happened upstream (caller) vs by us. Sampling at 10% should be fine.
alex_ng: On scoring format — do we return normalized scores [0..1], raw model logits, or both? And should we include model_id + quantization tag for provenance?
priya_chowdhury: Provide `score` (normalized) + optional `raw_score` if `include_raw=true`. Always include `model` and `model_variant` fields in response metadata. That helps debugging and routing.
jun_li: raw_score by default could bloat payloads for large fanouts. Make `include_raw` off by default. Also put an envelope like: {scores: [...], model: "rwd-v1.2", model_variant: "q4_0"}.
yuri: Also return `score_explanation` small enum for why candidate lost (e.g., "filtered", "score_too_low", "duplicate"). Helps console UX heatmaps.
kelsey: Console UX: when user clicks a route they should see estimated cost = sum(candidate_costs) + model_multiplier. Show a histogram of candidate counts seen in last 24h and a toggle to set `max_candidates` per route.
jun_li: Routing note: prefer model-affinity header -> route to warm pool for that model to avoid cold-start variance. Fallback to cheaper model variant if latency SLO is at risk. Need policy in config: `preferred_model, fallback_order, latency_budget_ms`.
alex_ng: Quota/units question — do we bill by scored candidate or by returned item? ops thinks scored candidate.
yuri: We log both `units_scored` and `units_returned`. Billing pipeline uses `units_scored` for cost. Console should expose both to help customers optimize.
priya_chowdhury: For safety, we should enforce hard `max_candidates` at API gateway (e.g., 1000) and surface a clear 400 with error code `too_many_candidates` if exceeded. For in-between, soft throttle that truncates and emits a `truncate` warning header.
ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: rerank-behavior-change -> canary rollout 10% at 2026-06-12T22:00Z. See #eng-releases for deploy ID 20260612-rr1. :robot_face:
kelsey: Canary plan — start with internal orgs + high-traffic read-only routes, run telemetry queries to ensure units_scored increase is expected and latency stable. If >5% p99 regress, auto rollback.
jun_li: One more: API shape suggestion — accept `candidates` as array OR a streaming attachment. For very large lists we should support chunked upload to avoid huge request mem. Console can show sample of first 100 candidates.
yuri: Telemetry sampling: full traces for errors and 0.1% of successful requests, aggregated metrics for candidate-distributions every minute. Add counters: `rerank.truncated`, `rerank.scored_count`, `rerank.fanout_distribution`.
alex_ng: Sounds like action items: 1) spec: default behavior = compute-all-up-to-hard-max, truncate + emit header/warn; 2) score envelope = normalized `score` + optional `raw_score`; always include model and variant; 3) telemetry events and console visuals (histogram, estimated cost); 4) gateway hard max + soft truncate; 5) rollout canary plan. I'll draft the RFC.
priya_chowdhury: Thanks — I'll add console mocks for the histogram and the truncation warning UI.
kelsey: I'll own the canary playbook.
jun_li: I'll sketch the proto change and cost calc formula.
yuri: I'll add telemetry queries and dashboard tiles.
ops-bot: Canary started: 10% -> 2026-06-12T22:00Z. Rollout ID 20260612-rr1.
alex_ng: Perfect — please comment on the RFC when I post. :thumbsup:
